core.notes:
Control Panel: in Basic, Profile Sync no longer shows a Companion tab beside it
A redesigned Control Panel, larger by default (1040 × 700). The sidebar has General, Appearance and Features (your modules, Tweaks and tools), then Feature settings: one settings page per module and Tweak, under Modules and Tweaks, in groups that fold and stay folded, and Development pinned at the bottom; the sidebar and the page scroll separately. Features lists Modules & Tweaks on one page and Tools on another, with the same columns; click a row for more about it (one at a time), Compact or Descriptions shows a short line under each name, and the ⚙ at the end of a row goes to its settings. Appearance opens on UI, with the themes as colour swatches, then Formatting, Menu, and Notifications (was Notices). Basic | Advanced is the first row of General. Setup is now the Welcome tour, one button under General › Welcome, Quick or Full on its first screen; General › Reset holds Reset settings and both window resets. In Basic, Updates also lists what changed.
The top-bar menu lists your Tweaks: click one to switch it on or off (with Undo), or its ⚙ to open its settings. Every Tweak starts in the menu
Profile Sync is under Development in the Control Panel again, in Basic too
Profile Sync now records when your VIP and QoL premium run out
The setup is larger and can be moved by its header: a Get started page, then General (theme, time zone, number format, Profile Sync) and Modules; Full adds Appearance and Top bar & pop-ups. The progress bar is at the bottom. Theme, fonts and UI scale show at once in the setup window (and the Control Panel), with an example; nothing else changes until Done.
Control Panel: a Basic | Advanced switch at the foot of the sidebar. New installs start in Basic, which shows the main options; if you already had AWOO+ you start in Advanced and see everything as before. The menu's search still finds every option and turns Advanced on to show it. Profile Sync's More options is now this switch.
Control Panel: drag to order Tools and Tweaks too, as modules; the menu and the welcome tour use that order. A module that is part of another is listed right under it.
Clearer names across the Control Panel, the menu and the tool settings: UI scale, Menu width, Text font and Number font, Number format and Number style, Sync automatically, Sync now, Bring windows on-screen and Reset window sizes (one button each, under General › Reset), Skip the tour, and Reset settings.
The short welcome tour now shows once for everyone, ticked as you have it now; a new install starts with a few picks ticked. Reset settings brings it back.
Profile Sync now reads each partner's stored XP in every skill, the figure in brackets beside the skill's level on the Partners page
New installs get a short setup: welcome, basics, modules. Later puts a Welcome button on the top bar; Control Panel › General › Start welcome tour opens it any time. Profile Sync explains itself in one line and shows a simple page with More options.
After this update, reload every open game tab once.
A Tweak can now be on from the first install; once you switch it off it stays off
Numbers and durations in every module follow your number format the same way.
Cost Tables: a tidier layout; your levels sit above the subject list, and nothing scrolls sideways on a phone.
Control Panel: each module, Tweak and tool says who made it, so you know who to send feedback to, and what it reads from Profile Sync and how fresh that is (click its row)
Profile Sync now records your cave tool levels, your house room levels, and your diamonds, meat, iron, wood and stone (shattered too)
A new calmer theme, Default, is now the default. It is light or dark as your device is set. If you picked a theme before, you keep it; choose Default in Appearance to switch
Modules no longer save to your browser when nothing they keep has changed (some saved the same thing every 10 seconds)
Profile Sync writes much less to your browser.
Turning a module off now also lets go of its Companion link, instead of keeping one more for every time it was turned on
Match game theme: windows stay solid when the game's own theme is see-through, instead of letting the game show through
Control Panel: open menus and sliders no longer reset while Profile Sync runs; table columns fit at any UI scale and sidebar width
Control Panel: a calmer, tidier look. One heading style, labels and values in one line from section to section, quieter table headings, and on a narrow screen the list moves above the page instead of anything scrolling sideways
Dungeon Win Rate: Dungeon Win Rate: an old scan no longer shows a doubled count on opening; the summary is worked out again from the saved results
Dungeon Win Rate: The newest and oldest attempt times now follow your General > Time zone setting (they used your computer's clock); the other numbers look the same
Dungeon Win Rate: Fixed an extra attempt being counted when two results share one card; long scans use less memory.
Sculpture Grid Overlay: Grid Overlay: the setting now picks how the overlay starts (rolls or item levels); the rotate button switches it while you play and turning the overlay on again starts from the setting
Sculpture Grid Overlay: Renamed Sculpture Grid Overlay (Grid Overlay for short). Your settings are kept
Sculpture Grid Overlay: On by default for new players; if you had it off, it stays off
Sculpture Grid Overlay: Rolls of 1,000% or more now have thousands separators.
Sculpture Grid Overlay: Now tells AWOO+ who made it (Weeble), shown when you click its row in the Control Panel's Features list
Sculpture Grid Overlay: No longer searches every page for the Highlight heading; it looks only on the sculpture page
